items.q: Why do you always have two temperatures?
items.a: Across the lifespan you have distinct **shell (skin)** and **core (organs/CNS)** temperatures. Skin TRP channels → spinal dorsal horn → lateral parabrachial → **POA (preoptic area)** drive sweating/vasodilation or amygdala-linked "get out" agitation.

**CNS neurons don't regenerate** — the safe heat window is narrow versus cold. Sauna is convenience, not magic: hot tub, layered clothing + jog, or wrestler "plastics" work if shell + core heat appropriately.

items.q: How often should you sauna for heart and longevity benefits?
items.a: Protocol: **80–100°C (176–212°F)**, 5–20 min/session. **2–3×/week → 27%** lower cardiovascular mortality vs 1×/week; **4–7×/week → 50%** lower (2018 BMC Medicine, n=1,688). Sitting sauna raises HR ~100–150 but is **not a substitute** for loaded exercise/bone density.

items.q: What cellular longevity pathways does heat trigger?
items.a: **Heat-shock proteins** rescue misfolded proteins. **FOXO3** (DNA repair, senescent-cell clearance) is upregulated with **2–7×/week** heat. Any deliberate heat likely hits multiple mechanisms — there is no protocol "only for cortisol" or "only for FOXO3."
**4× 12 min at ~90°C + 6 min ~10°C** water produced a significant cortisol drop (2021 study). Contrast is the lever — heat alone isn't framed as a cortisol-specific protocol.

items.q: How do you get the big growth-hormone spike?
items.a: **4× 30 min at 80°C same day** (2 hr total), **once/week max** (or ~every 10 days) → **16-fold GH** on day 1; attenuates with heat adaptation. Avoid food **2–3 hr before**; elevated glucose/insulin blunts GH.

items.q: Why is the discomfort part of the mood benefit?
items.a: Safe-but-uncomfortable heat releases **dynorphin** (κ receptor) → downstream **μ-opioid receptor upregulation** → elevated baseline mood and amplified joy. "A little bit of discomfort… is activating pathways that are allowing the **feel-good molecules**… to increase their efficiency."

items.q: When should you heat for sleep?
items.a: **Evening/later-day** heat aids post-exit cooling that parallels sleep-onset temperature drop (and supports GH). Cold right before bed can **raise core temp** and impair sleep.

items.q: How much should you rehydrate after sauna?
items.a: About **16 oz water per 10 min** in sauna; add electrolytes as needed. Treat heat sessions as real fluid loss, not optional sweat.
